title: Most Columbia River basalt erupted over 2.5 million years
body: The Columbia River Basalt Group records a series of lava flows in what is now the northwestern United States. Most accumulated between about 17 and 14.5 million years ago, laying one broad sheet of lava over another.
takeaway: A stack of rock layers can distinguish a long series of eruptions from one enormous event.
source: US Geological Survey, Columbia River Basalt Group
visual: a canyon wall exposing a thick stack of dark basalt layers
